text:
Rina: heads-up: p99 on /generate-us rose ~200ms shortly after the quota tweak last night. p50/p95 flat. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/latency-us
Vik: saw it. is this the new quota backoff that routes to cheaper-quant variants?
Rina: yes: fallback weight bumped to 0.4 at 01:05 UTC by autoscaler policy
Omar: quick trace check: ~80% of p99 samples hit model-quant and many have kvcache_miss on first chunk
Claire: model-quant median ok but tail worse for seq >500, so endpoint p99 sensitive when fallback increases
Vik: also suspicious: p99 calc used only ~160 samples last hour vs p95 ~9k. low sample p99s are noisy
Rina: so two factors: real tail shift from more quant hits + statistical noise from low p99 sample count
Omar: ops plan: rollback fallback weight -> 0.1 (Rina), run KV priming on canary (Omar), annotate dashboard with the quota-change (Vik)
Claire: UX ask: show sample_count next to each percentile and a low-sample warning when <500: tooltip "low samples -> percentile unstable"
Vik: backend: include per-shard sample counts in tdigest merge metadata so front-end can decide confidence
deploy-bot: Received rollback request from Rina. Rolling route us fallback weight -> 0.1
Rina: monitoring now. I'll post a short incident memo to #incidents with timeline + follow-ups
Omar: long-term: add per-variant percentile splits in endpoint pane and a provenance strip showing last routing/quota events
Claire: +1. document in routing playbook that routing to cheaper variants can increase endpoint tails; owners need to weigh SLO tradeoffs
Vik: will mock the sample-badge and a tiny expand chevron to show per-variant counts
Rina: thanks all. watch window 15m. if p99 doesn't drop we'll capture extended traces and run controlled traffic to isolate cache vs model behavior
